name: Dark Indigo
lede: Dark Indigo is a near-black violet-blue, ColorHub's library name for a darkened shade of [[indigo]], recorded only in the xkcd color survey of 2010.

sections.title: A darkened indigo
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark" plus the parent color [[indigo]] [1]. Unlike many of the library's darkened shades, it carries no Ridgway or ISCC-NBS filing; its only source is the crowd-sourced xkcd color survey of 2010, so its boundary against neighboring purples and blues rests on informal usage rather than an official dictionary [1]. On a monitor it reads as a deep violet rather than the blue-leaning indigo of the dye itself, which the [[indigo]] article covers separately [1].

The closest named neighbor on file is [[paua]], named for the iridescent shell, with [[midnight-blue]] and [[deep-blue]] both more vivid [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in only 7 of 23,781 paintings, among the rarer named shades in the collection, as photographed [2]. Every match comes from eighteenth-century British portrait miniatures, and the color plays only a shadow role where it appears [2]. The United Kingdom accounts for most of the matches, well above its average rate in our sample, which fits the concentration of matches in a single genre and period [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
